fresh_leads.qualification_text: you have learned in school in a driven, collaborative environment? Are you curious about electronic warfare (EW), radio frequency (RF) systems, national security, and having a real-world engineering impact? If so, we're looking for someone like you to join our team at APL! We are seeking curious and collaborative interns to contribute to the development, analysis, testing, and evaluation of current and next generation electronic warfare capabilities. Projects span many aspects of RF systems development and deployment, including RF hardware prototyping, modeling and simulation, test and evaluation, operational readiness, and reliability analysis. Interns will work alongside engineers, physicists, mathematicians, and scientists to gain experience across the development and evaluation process. This may include early analysis, simulation, laboratory testing, field testing, and technical communication. Our team values curiosity, collaboration, applied learning, and clear communication. Interns will also have opportunities to share their work through briefings with technical staff and project leaders! As an Electronic Warfare Systems intern, you will engage with our staff to... Model, analy ze, develop, integrate, and test RF and EW systems. Build software, algorithms, simulations, or data-analysis tools by applying principles from communications, signal processing, RF engineering, physics, mathematics, or computer science. Gain experience with laboratory systems that may include software-defined radios, antennas, embedded systems, signal generators, spectrum analyzers, and hardware-in-the-loop test environments. Support laboratory and field testing, analyze data, and communicate technical findings to the team. Qualifications You meet our minimum qualifications for the job if you have one or more of the following… Are pursuing a B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Electrical, Computer, Mechanical, or Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, or a related technical field. Are interested in RF systems, communications, signal processing, software, modeling and simulation, hardware, test and evaluation, or data analysis. Have strong communication skills and work effectively with technical team members and leaders. Have applied technical skills through coursework, research, projects, internships, or related activities. Have experience with at least one programming language or technical computing environment. Are willing to learn new math, physics, engineering, and computing concepts as needed for your work. Are able to obtain an Interim Secret level security clearance by your start date and can ultimately obtain a Secret level clearance. If selected, you will be subject to a government security clearance investigation and must meet the requirements for access to classified information. Eligibility requirements include U.S. citizenship. Have a minimum 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale. Note: When prompted to upload attachments, please include a copy of your college transcripts (unofficial transcripts are acceptable). You'll go above and beyond our minimum requirements if you... Have coursework, research, project, internship, or other experience with RF systems, communications, digital signal processing, radar, embedded systems, modeling and simulation, software development, or test and evaluation. Have experience programming in MATLAB, Python, C, C++, or a similar language. Have experience working with RF and electronics hardware such as software-defined radios, FPGAs, microcontrollers, antennas, or laboratory test equipment. Hold an active Secret or higher-level security clearance. About Us Why Work at APL?
